topics.name: Class and Object
topics.definition: A class is a blueprint that describes data and behavior. An object is a particular instance created from that class.
topics.example: If Car is a class with color and drive(), then myCar = new Car() creates an object of Car.

topics.name: Inheritance
topics.definition: Inheritance lets one Java class reuse and extend the fields and methods of another class.
topics.example: class Dog extends Animal gives Dog the accessible behavior of Animal and lets Dog add its own behavior.

topics.name: Polymorphism
topics.definition: Polymorphism means that the same method call or interface can have different behavior depending on the object or arguments.
topics.example: An Animal reference can refer to a Dog object, and calling sound() can run Dog's overridden implementation.

topics.name: Primary Key
topics.definition: A primary key is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a database table. Its values must be unique and not null.
topics.example: In a Students table, student_id can be the primary key because each student has a distinct ID.

topics.name: Foreign Key
topics.definition: A foreign key is a column or set of columns that refers to a key in another table, helping maintain relationships between rows.
topics.example: An Orders table can store customer_id as a foreign key that references Customers.customer_id.

topics.name: SQL JOIN
topics.definition: A SQL JOIN combines related rows from two or more tables using a matching condition.
topics.example: SELECT Students.name, Courses.title FROM Students JOIN Courses ON Students.course_id = Courses.id;

topics.name: Process and Thread
topics.definition: A process is a running program with its own execution resources. A thread is a path of execution within a process that shares the process's resources.
topics.example: A browser can run as a process with separate threads for its user interface, networking, and page work.

topics.name: Deadlock
topics.definition: A deadlock is a state where two or more processes wait indefinitely for resources held by one another.
topics.example: If Process A holds Resource 1 and waits for Resource 2, while Process B holds Resource 2 and waits for Resource 1, both can become stuck.

topics.name: Virtual Memory
topics.definition: Virtual memory gives each process an address space and lets the operating system use storage to support memory beyond currently available physical RAM.
topics.example: With paging, the operating system moves fixed-size memory pages between RAM and storage when needed.

topics.name: Artificial Intelligence
topics.definition: Artificial intelligence is the field of building computer systems that perform tasks associated with abilities such as reasoning, perception, language, or decision-making.
topics.example: A tutoring chatbot uses language models to interpret a student's question and generate an explanation.

topics.name: Machine Learning
topics.definition: Machine learning is a branch of AI in which a model learns patterns from data to make predictions or decisions, instead of being given every rule explicitly.
topics.example: A spam classifier can learn from labeled examples of spam and non-spam emails, then predict the class of a new email.

topics.name: Knowledge Representation
topics.definition: Knowledge representation is the way an AI system stores facts and relationships in a form that can be used to reason or answer questions.
topics.example: This project stores subject topics as JSON records containing a topic name, definition, example, and keywords.
